summary: Technical review of Module 02 (en). I re-ran every Python block in the concept and exercise files (21 blocks; e5 and e15 with Lab 1's first block in front). All printed outputs match the text. I recomputed the derivations and worked numbers independently: the sin 3x hinge table, the sawtooth counts, the GELU/SiLU minima and the tanh-approximation error, the saturation thresholds, Adam's bias-correction ratios, the heavy-ball and Nesterov step counts on the kappa = 100 ravine and the optimiser-paths widget defaults (179/110/126, 214 when rotated, Nesterov 55 at 0.025), the broadcasting trap (0.5174, std 0.0006), the s13 loop (epoch means, five seeds, 40.7%, logistic regression 59.2%), the fp32/fp16 facts, the e13 gradient-check medians and the e15 eta = 0.3 divergence. I also checked every concept claim that quotes a lab against the lab outputs, all cross-module links against the other modules' section lists, the citations, topic ownership (no 6N derivation; the FLOP and byte conventions are stated once with links; the M01 recalls are recalls) and the public-site rules (no hits). Each quiz question has exactly one defensible answer. 14 fixes: 6 wrong or imprecise numbers, 3 inaccurate claims, 3 notation or consistency fixes, 1 topic-ownership label, 1 broken reading task. check.mjs --module 2 --lang en: 0 errors, 0 warnings. 6 issues are reported below, 4 of them in the lab files.
changes: 10-concepts-a.md s1, worked example 'Twenty-two hinges for sin 3x' [number]: before 'the six slopes are (-2.304, 0.203, 2.524, 2.524, 0.203, -2.304), and the hinge coefficients are c = (-2.304, 2.508, ...)'; after '(-2.305, 0.203, 2.524, 2.524, 0.203, -2.305)' and 'c = (-2.305, 2.508, ...)'. s_0 = 3(sin(-2) - sin(-3)) = -2.30453, which rounds to -2.305; the drawn figure already shows -2.305.

10-concepts-a.md s3, 'Two consequences' [claim]: before 'Sigmoid networks of ten layers did not train in the 1990s for this reason'; after 'Deep sigmoid networks were notoriously hard to train in the 1990s largely for this reason'. The old sentence was an absolute historical claim.

10-concepts-a.md s2, 'Parameters, FLOPs and memory' [convention]: before 'Byte units, stated once for the series:'; after 'Byte units follow the series convention:'. Every module states the convention once, so it is not stated only here.

11-concepts-b.md s5, after 'Derivatives at a few points' [claim]: before 'The smooth activations have slopes above 1 right of the origin'; after 'The smooth activations have slopes above 1 for moderately large positive z (GELU beyond z = 0.75, SiLU beyond z = 1.28; SiLU'(1) is still 0.928)'. The table printed just above shows SiLU'(1) = 0.9277.

11-concepts-b.md fig-02-11 caption [number/figure]: before 'Heavy ball at eta = 0.07, mu = 0.9 moves smoothly, overshoots along the valley and spirals in'; after 'Heavy ball at eta = 0.015, mu = 0.9 (an effective rate eta/(1-mu) = 0.15) moves smoothly, ...'. At eta = 0.07 both heavy-ball modes contract only by sqrt(0.9) = 0.949 per step and the path leaves the plotted box. The SVG (src/figures/en/fig-02-11.svg) is drawn at eta = 0.015.
11-concepts-b.md s9, 'Schedules' [consistency]: before 'Figure 2.15 draws three schedules side by side.'; after '... on one set of axes.', as the figure caption says.

11-concepts-b.md s9, worked example 'The noise floor, predicted and measured' [topic ownership]: before 'With lambda = 1 and s^2/B = 1 the excess loss is'; after 'With lambda = 1 and s^2/B = 1, as in Module 01's example, the excess loss is'. The 0.0263 value repeats Module 01 s4's worked example, so the text now says it is a recall.

12-concepts-c.md s11, 'Early stopping' and worked example 'Early stopping in numbers' [notation]: before 'lambda_i/(lambda_i + alpha) theta*_i with alpha ~ 1/(eta t)' and 'alpha ~ 1/(0.01 x 1,000) = 0.1'; after 'lambda_i/(lambda_i + tau) theta*_i with tau ~ 1/(eta t), where tau is the coefficient of the penalty (tau/2)||theta||^2' and 'tau ~ ... = 0.1'. alpha is label smoothing's weight later in the same section, also with the value 0.1.

12-concepts-c.md s14, worked example 'A healthy run, per layer' [number]: before 'the gradients shrink by a factor of about twenty as the loss falls'; after 'by a factor of twenty to thirty-five'. Lab 4 gives 0.293/0.015 = 20, 0.350/0.010 = 35, 0.427/0.020 = 21, and Lab 4's own text says twenty to thirty-five.

12-concepts-c.md s14, answer to the 97.2% vs 97.8% check [number]: before 'The standard error of each is about 0.9 points'; after 'about 0.8 to 0.9 points'. sqrt(0.972*0.028/360) = 0.0087 and sqrt(0.978*0.022/360) = 0.0077.

40-practice.md, Glorot and Bengio 'After reading' [task design]: before 'with weights of variance 1/n_in, then 2/(n_in + n_out), then 0.01'; after 'with weights from the paper's "standard" initialisation U(-1/sqrt(n_in), 1/sqrt(n_in)) (variance 1/(3n_in)), then from its normalised initialisation (variance 2/(n_in + n_out)), then of variance 1'. At width 100 the three old scales are all 0.01, so the comparison showed nothing.

40-practice.md, Loshchilov and Hutter 'After reading' [claim]: before 'the paper multiplies the decay by a schedule multiplier, while PyTorch multiplies it by the current learning rate. Check that for a constant schedule the two agree'; after 'the paper multiplies its decay lambda by the schedule multiplier eta_t alone, while PyTorch multiplies its weight_decay by the current learning rate, which is the base rate alpha times eta_t. Work out which weight_decay reproduces the paper's lambda, and check that under a cosine schedule both decays shrink with the schedule.' With a constant schedule they do not agree unless weight_decay = lambda/alpha (Algorithm 2: theta <- theta - eta_t(alpha m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+eps) + lambda theta)).

40-practice.md, Summary [claim]: before 'fp16 overflows above 65,504 and needs loss scaling, while bf16'; after 'fp16 overflows above 65,504 and needs loss scaling to keep small gradients from underflowing, while bf16'. Loss scaling is for underflow, not overflow.
issues: Lab 4, Step 1 (21-labs-b.md), text after the first block: 'In this data set the corner pixels are almost always blank.' The block prints the constant pixels [0, 24, 32, 39]. Only pixel 0 is a corner; 24 and 32 are on the left edge (rows 3 and 4) and 39 on the right edge (row 4). Fix: 'In this data set some border pixels (the top-left corner and the middle of the left and right edges) are almost always blank.'

Lab 3, Step 5 (20-labs-a.md), fourth observation: 'Adam is not faster than well-tuned momentum SGD in reaching a training loss of 0.1 (epoch 4, against 3 for SGD at 0.5)'. The comparison names momentum SGD but cites plain SGD at 0.5, and momentum 0.9 at 0.05 also takes epoch 4. Fix: 'Adam is not faster than well-tuned SGD in reaching a training loss of 0.1 (epoch 4, against 3 for SGD at 0.5 and for Nesterov momentum)'.

Lab 5, 'What you should see' (21-labs-b.md): 'Logging the initial loss and the gradient norm costs one line each and diagnoses two of the four bugs; the third is diagnosed by evaluating twice.' This leaves script A unaccounted for. Fix: '... diagnoses two of the four bugs (C and B); D is found by evaluating twice, and A by its loss floor of 1.46.'

Lab 1, Try this 3 (20-labs-a.md): 'fit the neo-Hookean nominal stress ... of Module 01, Section 12 (c_1 = 0.5 MPa, stretches lambda from 0.6 to 1.0, 2% noise)'. Module 01 s12 and its Lab 5 use c_1 = 10 kPa (stretches 0.975 to 0.600, sigma 0.05 kPa plus 2%). Not wrong, but to tie the two modules together use 'c_1 = 10 kPa, stretches from 0.6 to 1.0, 2% noise'.

Figure numbering (not a lab issue): the plan's fig-02-14 (AdamW versus L2 shrinkage), fig-02-16 (range-test curves) and fig-02-19 (float-format number lines) were dropped in the edit pass. Because build numbers figures from their ids, the page shows Figures 2.13, 2.15, 2.17, 2.18, 2.20 and 2.21, with gaps at 2.14, 2.16 and 2.19. Either draw the three figures or renumber the remaining ids and their references (Figure 2.15, 2.17, 2.18, 2.20, 2.21 in the text and the figure files).

Not verified by re-running: the mlp-playground numbers in s1 ('The playground in numbers', the eight-seed spread) and the dead-unit example in s5. They come from a NumPy simulation of the widget specification that is not in the module. They agree with the plan's reference behaviour and are labelled as simulation numbers. Note also that the s8 parameter-group snippet ('25856 266') uses a `model` it does not define. As a concept-text snippet this is acceptable, but it fails if run on its own.
